name: Army bandage
description: Sterile pressure dressing. Stops a light bleed; good for two.

name: Esmarch tourniquet
description: Rubber strap. Stops a heavy bleed, wherever it is.

name: CAT tourniquet
description: One-handed combat tourniquet. Stops a heavy bleed, twice, quicker than an Esmarch.

name: CALOK-B hemostatic applicator
description: Hemostatic granules in a syringe. Stops a light or heavy bleed in two seconds; three uses.

name: Immobilizing splint
description: Wooden splint and gauze. Sets one fractured arm or leg.

name: Aluminium splint
description: Mouldable aluminium splint. Sets a fracture fast, three times over.

name: Analgin painkillers
description: Takes the edge off for a minute and a half: no pain, and a broken leg can run again. Four doses.

name: Ibuprofen tablets
description: Strong painkillers: four minutes without pain a dose, six doses. Thirsty work.

name: AI-2 medkit
description: Small army medkit. Heals one body part a use from a 100 HP pool; does nothing for bleeds.

name: Car first aid kit
description: Small medkit from a glovebox. 220 HP to heal with; stopping a light bleed costs 50 of it.

name: Salewa first aid kit
description: Large medkit: 400 HP, stops light bleeds (45 HP) and heavy bleeds (175 HP).

name: IFAK individual first aid kit
description: Compact large medkit: 300 HP in one cell, stops light (30 HP) and heavy bleeds (210 HP).

name: AFAK tactical first aid kit
description: Best kit that fits a pocket: 400 HP, stops light (30 HP) and heavy bleeds (170 HP), quick to use.

name: Grizzly medical kit
description: Field hospital in a bag: 1,800 HP, stops light (40 HP) and heavy bleeds (130 HP) and sets fractures (50 HP). Slow to work through.

name: CMS surgical kit
description: Field surgery on a blacked limb or stomach: brings it back at 35% HP, but it loses 35% of its max HP for the rest of the raid. 14 seconds at a crawl. Three uses.

name: Surv12 field surgical kit
description: Proper surgical set: a blacked part comes back at 50% HP, losing only 20% of its max HP. Ten seconds, eight uses.
